Thanks Irene — thrilled to be moving forward. - Training for 12 engineers across two cohorts (recordings required)

We have procurement kickoff on Sep 10; it'd be helpful to show a committed plan before then.

Thanks — Sam

Sam — great to hear, congrats on the close. I put together a working MAP below that covers governance, canary cadence, migration cutover windows, and training. This is a proposed plan so we can iterate quickly ahead of your procurement call.

High level (proposed):
- Week 0 (provisioning): Reserved Dedicated pool provisioned; baseline perf tests (internal).
- Week 1–4 (canary): 2-phase canary. Phase A: internal traffic + 10% external on dedicated; Phase B: progressive rollout to 50% with metrics gates.
- Week 5 (validation & training): Final load test, training cohort 1 + recorded session.
- Week 6 (migration & cutover): Incremental migration of production routes; contingency rollback plan.

Acceptance criteria (short list):
- 95th percentile tail latency < 350ms for gen calls at expected QPS
- Token error-rate < 0.3% over 24h rolling window
- No more than 1 P1 incident requiring immediate rollback during canary

I have attached the MAP PDF and a canary checklist Karthik and I prepared. Karthik — can you confirm the KV-cache warmup approach and the cadence for canary traffic shifts? Marissa — I'll need training slots and a short registration link for the two cohorts.

I'll update the MAP with any procurement constraints after your Sep 10 call.

Best,
Irene
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Irene / Sam — quick technical confirmation from the runtime side.

Canary plan specifics (engineer-facing):
- Phase A (Days 1–7): internal traffic + shadowing 10% external. KV cache priming: run 6-hour prefix replay on a mirrored pool; expected steady-state warmup ~18–24 hours.
- Traffic shift increments: 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 72-hour intervals provided the following gates pass: 95p latency, error-rate, and model output quality check (sampled prompts).
- Rollback criteria: any 95p latency breach >25% above baseline for 2 consecutive measurement windows (1 hour) OR token error-rate >0.5% over 30 minutes.

Operational notes:
- We'll attach a small tracer to the first two routes to measure KV cache hit rates; if hit < 65% after 24h, we pause expansion and triage.
- Canary runbook attached: helio-canary-checklist.xlsx. It includes exact curl commands, alert thresholds, and rollback steps.

I'll own the on-call rotation for the canary window and will be available for the Sep 10 procurement call to confirm technical gating language.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Sam — looping in training details. Proposed schedule to hit your request for two cohorts (12 engineers):
- Cohort A (hands-on): Week 3, 2-hour live session (max 8 attendees) — deep dive on routing policies, observability, and canary troubleshooting.
- Cohort B (ops-focused): Week 4, 90-minute session — runbook walkthrough + practice rollback.
- Deliverables: recordings, quick-start runbook, 1 pager for execs, office hours (2x 1-hour sessions during Week 5).

I'll send a registration form (simple Google Form) after you confirm attendee emails. Also included a training-cadence.csv with proposed dates and instructor assignments.

Acceptance QA: we will run a final acceptance demo in Week 5 where HelioSys will validate two end-to-end flows: a generation request and an embedding retrieval under load. If both pass, we mark the MAP "Operationally Accepted" and proceed to migration.

Regards,
